meta: Engineered to honour history - the HAVOC 1917 marks the 110th Anniversary of the battle of Cambrai and the enduring legacy of the Royal Tank Regiment

short.x: Built to honour history. Engineered to endure.
The HAVOC 1917 marks the 110th Anniversary of the battle of Cambrai – commemorating the battlefield that defined the future of armoured warfare and the enduring legacy of the Royal Tank Regiment.

Inspired by the rugged practicality, precision, and resilience of military equipment, the HAVOC 1917 combines commemorative significance with everyday capability. Designed as a wear every day watch, it reflects the spirit of those who pioneered armoured warfare while delivering dependable performance for modern life.

The 42mm stainless steel case provides exceptional strength and durability while remaining balanced and comfortable for daily wear. Protecting the dial is a sapphire crystal, chosen for its outstanding scratch resistance and lasting clarity ensuring the watch remains ready for years of service and wear. With 100 metres of water resistance, the HAVOC 1917 is built to perform in demanding conditions, whether navigating the outdoors, travelling, or everyday use.

Powering the watch is the trusted NH35 automatic movement, selected for its proven reliability and durability. Driven by the motion of the wearer, it requires no battery and continues the tradition of mechanical dependability.
The HAVOC 1917 comes with both a stainless steel bracelet and a soft feel silicone rubber strap, delivering comfort, durability, and the ability to dress up or down for any occasion.

desc.x: The HAVOC 1917 is a tribute to the Royal Tank Regiment, celebrating the pioneering spirit of those who fought at Cambrai and shaped the future of armoured warfare. It embodies the determination, courage, and innovation that define the Regiment’s history – making it a timepiece that honours those who have served with the world’s oldest tank regiment and resonates with enthusiasts who admire their legacy.

True to the Regiment’s ethos, the HAVOC 1917 combines dependable automatic performance with versatile straps in both steel and silicone, allowing wearers to reflect the discipline and adventurous spirit of the Tank Regiment in every situation.

Built around a 42mm stainless-steel case, the Challenger delivers a strong wrist presence without unnecessary bulk. A scratch-resistant sapphire crystal protects the dial, while the Japanese automatic GMT movement provides dependable mechanical performance without the need for a battery.

The dial carries a distinctive subdued Union Flag design, giving the Challenger its British identity without overpowering the watch. Contrasting GMT detailing provides fast identification of the second time zone while maintaining the clean, functional aesthetic expected from HAVOC.

Drawing inspiration from years of operational experience working alongside the legendary A-10 Thunderbolt II (“Warthog”), the HAVOC JTAC pays tribute to those who have directed devastating close air support missions in some of the world’s harshest environments. The A-10’s ability to deliver accurate firepower in support of troops on the ground has made it one of the most respected aircraft ever to serve alongside JTACs.
Built with the same philosophy of reliability and precision, the HAVOC JTAC is designed to perform anywhere—from the mountains to the ocean, from everyday wear to demanding expeditions.

short.x: HAVOC OP HERRICK – Military-Inspired Commemorative Tool Watch
The HAVOC OP HERRICK is more than a military-inspired tool watch. It has been designed as a lasting tribute to the British servicemen and women who served in Afghanistan during Operation HERRICK.

Built around a rugged 42mm black PVD-coated titanium case, the OP HERRICK combines lightweight strength, reliability and military heritage with a unique physical connection to operations in Afghanistan.

At the heart of the design is a brass movement holder manufactured using brass from a 105mm artillery shell fired at Roshan Tower, Musa Qala, Afghanistan. The round was fired in support of British troops operating in the area, giving every OP HERRICK watch a tangible connection to the history and service that inspired it.

The lightweight titanium case features a fixed-lug design, a feature traditionally associated with military watches because of its strength and strap security. Its black PVD coating gives the watch a purposeful, understated appearance while complementing the Afghanistan-inspired dial.

Protecting the dial is sapphire crystal glass, providing excellent scratch resistance and long-term clarity. With 200 metres of water resistance, the OP HERRICK has been designed as a genuine everyday tool watch rather than simply a commemorative piece.

Powering the watch is the proven Japanese NH35 automatic movement, widely recognised for its durability and reliability. Powered by the movement of the wearer, it requires no battery and provides a dependable mechanical platform suited to the character of the watch.
The OP HERRICK is fitted with a single-pass black rubber NATO-style strap, providing additional security through the fixed lugs while remaining comfortable and practical for everyday use.
Each watch can also be individually laser engraved on the caseback with the owner’s ZAP number, creating a personal connection between the watch and the individual who served.
The result is a watch designed not simply to reference military service, but to preserve a small piece of Operation HERRICK history.

short.x: The Brough Superior SS80 is one of the most celebrated motorcycles ever built – earning its enviable reputation through exceptional engineering, performance, and exclusivity. Introduced in the 1920s by George Brough, the SS80 combined hand-built craftsmanship with reliability that set new standards for British motorcycling.

Brough Superior motorcycles were favoured by military officers, adventurers, and wealthy enthusiasts – most famously T.E. Lawrence (Lawrence of Arabia), who owned several examples. The SS80’s rugged British engineering and association with prominent military figures have cemented its place as an icon of Britain’s motoring heritage.

The HAVOC SS80 is a prestigious collaboration between Brough Superior GB Limited and HAVOC Watches Ltd to celebrate this legendary vehicle. Crafted in striking bronze and powered by an automatic movement, this exceptional timepiece combines heritage engineering with modern craftsmanship.

Limited to just 80 pieces worldwide, the SS80 is a rare collector’s watch designed for enthusiasts of both horology and iconic British motorcycling history. Demand for this unique timepiece is exceptionally strong – secure yours before this exclusive edition sells out.

desc.x: Inspired by the legendary Brough Superior SS80 motorcycle, the HAVOC SS80 pays tribute to one of Britain’s most revered machines – a hand-built icon celebrated for its performance, prestige, and historic value. The watch captures the spirit of this remarkable vehicle in a distinctive bronze case, blending mechanical craftsmanship with unmistakable British character.

Created exclusively in partnership with Brough Superior GB Limited, the HAVOC SS80 is limited to just 80 pieces worldwide. For collectors of fine watches and historic motorcycles alike, it represents a rare opportunity to own the only timepiece in the world authorised by one of the most famous names in motorcycling.
